body:
tl;dr; my understanding is that the issue reported here is about arguments of the `ngOnChanges` callback.

@luke-emmental thnx for the reproduce scenario. I had a brief look at it and I must say that it is not 100% clear to me what is the observed vs. expected behaviour. Let me explain.

II've simplified a bit your scenario (mostly coping things to one file) here: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-input-change-issue-47nx1a?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.component.ts

I've just copied part of the scenario that you've marked as "this is not problem" but for me there is problem in this part as well :-) More precisely:
* expected: only `timeIn` is reported in `ngOnChanges`
* observed: both `objIn` (incorrect) and  `timeIn` (correct) is reported in `ngOnChanges`

There is definitively something going on here with `ngOnChanges` but I'm trying to be very precise about the scenario here. Could you guide me a bit more here on what is expected vs. observed?

expected: only timeIn is reported in ngOnChanges
observed: both objIn (incorrect) and timeIn (correct) is reported in ngOnChanges
---- 
@pkozlowski-opensource  Yes! My intention is correct. Thank you!

I found `this is not problem` reason

in your case using `template`
my case using `templateUrl`

The two cases give different results.

> The two cases give different results.

I don't see any difference in the observed behavior between the two reproductions above. The second one is a bit simpler.

Hmm, I have found an appropriate workaround there, just passing `asyncTimer` as `Object` without extracting a value.
https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-input-change-issue-ztz4kh?file=src/app/app.component.ts

> The two cases give different results.

 umm... sorry.  It was wrong

@destus90 ha! I think that you are onto something! I've just observed that just removing `?` also makes things work as expected. That is, replacing `[timeIn]="(ayncTimer|async)?.t` with `[timeIn]="(ayncTimer|async).t` <- notice lack of ?) gets us to the expected value in the `OnChanges` callback (it will error initially as the first emitted value is `null` but then it starts to work OK: https://stackblitz.com/edit/angular-ivy-input-change-issue-vnypga?file=src/app/app.component.ts

To sum up, `ngOnChanges` is over-reporting changes under some circumstances. In the reproduction scenario it means that:
* `[timeIn]="(ayncTimer|async)?.t` - is WRONG (expected notification with `timeIn`, actual notification with `timeIn` and `objIn`)
* `[timeIn]="(ayncTimer|async).t` is OK (expected notification with `timeIn` only)


It is not clear to me if this is a compiler bug (we are generating different code for the 2 above cases) or the runtime bug. This will need more root-cause analysis but at this point it looks to me like a confirmed bug in ivy.
